newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives lag Labour by 22 points - Poll.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives lag Labour by 22 points - Poll.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative Party trails the opposition Labour Party by 22 points, according to an opinion poll published by MORI on Monday.
The Mori poll, carried out for the Sun newspaper, showed Conservative support at 30 percent, compared with 52 percent for Labour and 13 percent for the Liberal Democrats.

The MORI poll also found that 64 percent of those polled were against a single European currency and 22 percent in favour, with 40 percent backing withdrawal from the European Union and 44 percent in favour of staying in.

A parallel MORI poll for the Sun found support for Prime Minister John Major's Party had collapsed in Basildon, the south-east England constituency which gave the first indication of the Conservatives' surprise victory in the 1992 general election.

The Sun poll, carried out among 548 adults last week, found support for the Tories in Basildon had plummeted to 24 percent from 45 percent at the 1992 general election. Support for Labour had risen to 61 percent from 42 percent at the last election.
